races.name: HKJC Worldpool Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: True Test
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who is likely to secure an uncontested lead; William Buick provides a significant upgrade in class of ride, though a style-fit flag at this trip and distance suggests her chance depends heavily on whether the pace she sets is genuinely sustainable rather than too slow to protect her.

runners_data.name: Machadadorp
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding has 11 winners from 55 runners over the past 14 days and this filly arrives in fine form having won her last two starts at seven furlongs on Good ground — Oisin Murphy's booking is notable and she is best placed to capitalise if the pace suits prominent racers.

runners_data.name: Ruby's Angel
runners_data.note: Has shown sharp form at six furlongs and steps up slightly in trip here; her recent Yarmouth win came on Good ground and she is likely to push forward under Clifford Lee, but the step from six to seven furlongs on fast ground is a small query given all five historical runs sit at six furlongs or shorter.

runners_data.name: Shallow
runners_data.note: Wears headgear (p) and has a tidy record of placing at six and seven furlongs on Good, though her single win from 15 similar-going runs reflects a horse who runs her race consistently without always converting; Saffie Osborne holds the ride and her hold-up style meshes well with this controlled-pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Planet Seeker
runners_data.note: Jamie Spencer takes over and this filly won at six furlongs on Good at Goodwood on her most recent form-line win; a genuine front-runner by nature, she faces the challenge of finding herself pushed into midfield by the race shape, which is not where she produces her best work.

runners_data.name: Tarot
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's filly carries a headgear flag (h) and has been placed at six and seven furlongs, including on Good ground; she is naturally a horse that wants to race prominently, and being crowded out of that position by True Test and the other pace horses will leave her racing against type and reduces her scenario probability accordingly.

runners_data.name: Havana Pusey
runners_data.note: A six-year-old carrying top weight of 142lbs for John Gallagher; her best form this season has come at seven furlongs on Good ground and she owns a recent win at this exact trip and going combination, making her profile structurally attractive in a controlled-pace race from a hold-up style.

runners_data.name: Song N Dance
runners_data.note: Has been running over a mile but clearly acts on Good ground and has winning form at seven furlongs; Tom Marquand takes the ride for Stuart Woods and her record of five places from eight similar-going runs suggests she finds ways to be involved without always dominating, useful if the pace stretches the field.

runners_data.name: Just A Girl
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's filly has an exceptional record of finishing second in five of her last seven starts at seven furlongs on Good, suggesting she produces her run consistently late; Billy Loughnane is booked and her pattern screams that she needs something to race off — the controlled True Test-led tempo is precisely the scenario that allows her to close with purpose.

races.paceDynamic: True Test is the confirmed pace-setter here and, with only one genuine front-runner in the field, she is likely to enjoy an uncontested lead at a fair but manageable gallop on Good to Firm ground over seven furlongs at Newmarket. Machadadorp, Ruby's Angel, and Song N Dance will press forward to occupy the prominent berths behind her, ensuring the race is run at a respectable tempo without degenerating into a dawdle. The field carries more naturally prominent types than the race shape can accommodate — Planet Seeker and Tarot are true front-rank horses who will find themselves shuffled into midfield against their instincts, compromising their ability to produce their best. With one leader setting a controlled, honest pace, this race shape favours hold-up horses who can travel smoothly in the slipstream and produce a sustained late run into the Newmarket dip — Just A Girl, Havana Pusey, and Shallow are the profiles most structurally aligned with what this setup creates.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If True Test sets an honest but uncontested gallop and the hold-up runners track smoothly through the dip.
scenarios.body: True Test's single-leader scenario means the pace is sustainable rather than punishing, and the strong finishers who have been conserving energy will have full fuel reserves approaching the final furlong; the Newmarket straight rewards those who switch off early and hit top gear late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Rail Gallop
scenarios.trigger: If Machadadorp or Ruby's Angel push up aggressively early to pressurise True Test and the pace becomes genuinely strong.
scenarios.body: A quicker early tempo would string the field out and favour runners who can maintain high-speed cruise from a handy position rather than closing from the rear; those locked into a rhythm near the front would simply outstay the hold-up horses if the last quarter is run at an even pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Front Runs Clear
scenarios.trigger: If True Test is allowed to dictate at a very modest early tempo and the field fails to press, letting her coast home.
scenarios.body: A slow-run race over Newmarket's straight seven becomes a test of natural speed and punch from the front rather than stamina, rewarding the leader if she simply slows the race to a canter and kicks clear unchallenged in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Redistributed Types Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Planet Seeker or Tarot manage to wrestle a forward position and dominate from the front against expectations.
scenarios.body: This is a low-probability shape precisely because both horses carry redistribution flags and are likely to find themselves out of position in a field with genuine pace ahead of them; if somehow the race shape inverts and they do get to the front, their natural front-running class could be decisive.

watchPoints.text: True Test and Buick set the pace — watch whether the gallop through the first three furlongs is genuine or whether the field allows her to steal an uncontested crawl, as that fundamentally changes whether the closers can get to her.

Planet Seeker and Tarot are both natural front-runners who have been mapped to midfield; if Jamie Spencer or Marco Ghiani attempt to push forward early to reclaim their natural position, a messy pace battle could develop in the first furlong that disrupts the entire field's rhythm.

Just A Girl has finished second in five of her last seven runs at this course and distance — watch whether Loughnane angles her wide for a clear run in the final two furlongs or whether she gets boxed behind the prominent runners, as that has cost her at least two recent wins.

Havana Pusey carries 142lbs top weight but has a strong record when fresh over 35 days and has won twice at this course and distance on similar going — weight is the key variable to monitor against the otherwise strong profile fit.

Shallow's headgear and consistent placing record at six and seven furlongs on Good make her a reliable each-way profile, but her single win from 15 similar-going runs is a structural ceiling worth noting before assigning her scenario-winning probability.

races.name: Weatherbys Handicap

runners_data.name: Wechaad
runners_data.note: Roger Varian three-year-old who showed his best form winning over 7f on soft, stepping up to a mile here; Ryan Moore gives him a tactical upgrade and he has the form to race prominently in his natural style, though this Good to Firm surface is slightly faster than his optimum.

runners_data.name: Sunset On Leros
runners_data.note: Marco Botti's hold-up specialist wearing a hood, with creditable placed efforts over a mile on good ground; Marco Ghiani rides and the horse will need the pace to develop late, with a trip back to a mile looking a logical move after running too freely at longer distances.

runners_data.name: St Anton
runners_data.note: Won back-to-back over a mile on good ground and clearly has the form to be competitive, but his natural front-running instincts mean he is highly likely to push forward from his mapped midfield position — Pat Dobbs will have to manage him carefully if the prominent slots are already taken by Tales Of Wisdom and others.

runners_data.name: Wild Thoughts
runners_data.note: Four consecutive victories including three over a mile on good or standard ground make Wild Thoughts's form credentials strong, but he is a horse that likes to race on or near the pace and Saffie Osborne will face a genuine tactical dilemma in a field where prominent positions are at a premium; his STYLE_FIT flag reflects real risk.

runners_data.name: Alfaraz
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's charge won last time over a mile on good ground and clearly appreciates this trip and surface, with Oisin Murphy a big booking; his natural style pushes him toward the front but with several rivals seeking the same ground he may find himself further back than ideal, which is not a straightforward scenario for him.

runners_data.name: Eklleem
runners_data.note: William Haggas runner who landed his maiden over a mile at Kempton last time and has William Haggas's powerful form record behind him; Tom Marquand rides and the horse's prominent inclinations will be squeezed in this field, meaning he may have to settle for a position he is not entirely comfortable with.

runners_data.name: Tales Of Wisdom
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter in this race, having led throughout to win over a mile on good ground, and William Buick's controlled style suits dictating from the front; the STYLE_FIT tag reflects that he is at the head of a deep prominent group rather than genuinely alone, and he carries top weight of 135lbs as OR=99.

runners_data.name: Moonfall
runners_data.note: George Boughey's progressive three-year-old won last time over a mile at Kempton and has an excellent record on good ground with Billy Loughnane continuing the partnership; races prominently in a style that exactly suits this shape, and his course form (he handles the Rowley Mile's straight demands) is a notable plus.

runners_data.name: Iron Lily
runners_data.note: Mrs John Harrington's filly arrives on the back of two below-par efforts over 7f-8f on good ground, and the 68 days off is the longest absence in the field; James Doyle takes over in the saddle and she will operate from off the pace, needing a truly run race to get competitive after those disappointing recent showings.

races.paceDynamic: Tales Of Wisdom is the confirmed front-runner here, and with William Buick in the saddle for Charlie Appleby, he is expected to set a controlled, honest gallop on Good to Firm ground over this Rowley Mile — sustainable rather than suicidal, creating a race run at a measured tempo that will not string the field out early. Behind him, Wechaad and Moonfall are genuine prominent types who should slot in comfortably just off the pace, while St Anton, Wild Thoughts, Alfaraz, and Eklleem are all true front-running or prominent horses by nature but are mapped to midfield because there are simply more pace-inclined runners than the race shape can accommodate at the front — of those, St Anton and Wild Thoughts are most likely to actually push forward and contest for position behind Tales Of Wisdom given their strong recent front-running profiles. This field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all get their natural position, which compresses the midfield and leaves genuine hold-up horses (Sunset On Leros, Iron Lily) with cleaner air late but also further to travel. A controlled pace from Tales Of Wisdom with a compact group tracking him favours horses who can race prominently without expending early energy — the prominent-to-midfield stalkers who travel fluently and produce a sustained finish will be best served by this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Tales Of Wisdom sets a measured pace and the race develops into a conventional front-to-midfield contest on Good to Firm ground.
scenarios.body: Tales Of Wisdom dictates from the front at a sustainable tempo, and the horses tracking him in second and third — Wechaad, Moonfall, and potentially St Anton — are perfectly placed to pounce in the final furlong without having had to fight for position; the Good to Firm surface rewards those travelling smoothly rather than grinding from the rear.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Hold-Up Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely slow enough that a late rush from behind proves decisive in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A dawdling tempo keeps the field compressed until the two-furlong pole, at which point Sunset On Leros and Iron Lily get to unleash their late runs with momentum that the prominent types cannot match; Sunset On Leros's form over a mile at Goodwood and Iron Lily's class make them the most likely beneficiaries of a truly run-to-order finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Fractures, Front Stays
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves strong enough to stretch the field but Tales Of Wisdom proves difficult to reel in and the true prominent horses exhaust themselves chasing.
scenarios.body: A genuinely honest pace from Tales Of Wisdom burns off those who fought for prominent positions — St Anton, Wild Thoughts, and others who are out of natural role — while Tales Of Wisdom, controlled by Buick, proves a thorough stayer who holds on under pressure; Moonfall, having won last time out from a handy position, may be the only one with the class and position to mount a serious late challenge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Scrappy Pace Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If early position-jockeying among the numerous prominent types creates uneven fractions, disrupting rhythm for most of the field.
scenarios.body: Multiple horses fighting for the limited prominent positions behind Tales Of Wisdom — particularly Eklleem, Wild Thoughts, and Alfaraz — cause messy early exchanges that unsettle their own races; in this case a horse ridden cold and delivered late such as Sunset On Leros or a cool-headed jockey like Oisin Murphy on Alfaraz benefits from staying out of trouble.

watchPoints.text: Tales Of Wisdom leads but carries top weight (135lbs) against a field packed with prominent types — if St Anton or Wild Thoughts press him from early, his ability to control the pace and conserve energy for the finish could be compromised significantly.

St Anton and Wild Thoughts are both true prominent horses mapped to midfield due to overcrowding — watch the first two furlongs closely to see whether they push forward anyway, because if they do the race shape could become materially more pressured than anticipated.

Iron Lily's 68-day absence is the longest in the field and her last two performances were poor; watch her in the market — if she drifts significantly pre-race, treat her late-run chance as low probability regardless of Good to Firm suitability.

Moonfall is the one prominent-type runner who should get his position cleanly — he is not redistributed and Boughey/Loughnane have him in form; watch whether he travels smoothly in second or third, as his position at the two-furlong pole will be a key tell for the race.

The pace dynamic shifts materially if Buick elects to drop Tales Of Wisdom in and ride conservatively rather than lead — if Tales Of Wisdom does not go to the front from the stalls, the race loses its confirmed setter and the scenario probabilities compress across the board.

races.name: Betway Bunbury Cup (Heritage Handicap)

runners_data.name: Colombier
runners_data.note: Consistent at 7f on good ground but six-year-old form has been patchy (three placed runs from nine on similar going, no win), and the headgear note is relevant — likely to race prominently as usual from stall position.|

runners_data.name: Dark Tornado
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse with a solitary win from thirteen runs on good or similar ground, though his one win in this dataset came over 7f at Newmarket — J F Egan rides and Wigham's yard is in sharp form (4 from 5 in 14 days), making him the standout late-threat candidate.|

runners_data.name: The Fingal Raven
runners_data.note: Won at 8f on good and has placed form over 7f, but the OR drop and 23-day absence after a flat run (16th at Newmarket) are concerns; Jamie Osborne's yard is cold (0 from 15 in 14 days), which is a material negative here.|

runners_data.name: Back In Black
runners_data.note: Fanshawe yard is active and winning (5/23 in 14 days), and the horse has solid placed form on good ground — but he is a natural prominent racer who the pace map pushes into midfield given the crowded front rank, so his ability to express his style is compromised at the forecast race shape.|

runners_data.name: Supido
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore booking lifts the profile; one recent win from 13 on similar going suggests he finds it hard to win but is consistent, and his hold-up style is genuinely suited to a scenario where the lead group ties up in the final furlong.|

runners_data.name: Christian David
runners_data.note: Hannon runner who has placed form over 8f on good but all recent wins came at a mile — the front-rank squeeze in this field means this natural prominent horse is likely displaced further back than ideal, softening his chance despite the decent placed record.|

runners_data.name: Nostrum
runners_data.note: Appleby horses have had quiet 14 days (2/23) and Nostrum has no wins from 15 runs on comparable going — a hold-up type whose form figures (0, 2, 5, 8, 14) suggest flashes without landing the blow.|

runners_data.name: Aalto
runners_data.note: William Buick is a major positive in any analysis, and Aalto's last run was a close second over this exact trip on good — he is a natural hold-up horse who the map shifts slightly forward, but the key angle is that Buick can produce him late with a clear run.|

runners_data.name: Physique
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 7f on good and has placed at 8f on good ground, so form and going both stack up — a genuine front-rank racer who cannot get that position in this field, which is the single biggest risk to his chance despite the uptick in form.|

runners_data.name: Dapper Guest
runners_data.note: Margarson yard is cold (0/5 in 14 days), the OR of 80 is modest, and the visor headgear hasn't unlocked consistent form — hold-up in style but mapped to midfield; very limited winning prospects in this grade.|

runners_data.name: Royal Zabeel
runners_data.note: Highest OR in the field at 102 and a 7f Newmarket winner on good, so course-and-distance form is directly relevant; the 5lb claimer Conor Whiteley (5) is a concern in a competitive handicap at this level, and only seven days since last run.|

runners_data.name: Two Tribes
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner ridden by Oisin Murphy — recent form is a string of zeros after earlier wins at 6f, and the step up to 7f at Newmarket may stretch his ability to quicken off his own pace; his STYLE_FIT flag notes he could be racing slightly out of role if the trip catches him out.|

runners_data.name: Elarak
runners_data.note: Consistent at 7f on good ground with three wins from nine on similar going and two seconds; Charles Hills yard is in fair nick, Billy Loughnane has been in form, and the horse profiles as the most natural prominent-tracker who can also win — strong fit for the dominant scenario.|

runners_data.name: Great Acclaim
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's horse has been placed four times from eleven on good ground at 7f and loves this course — the form figures (3,2,3) over 7f at Newmarket in good conditions are the most consistent in the field for this exact scenario.|

runners_data.name: Witch Hunter
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up horse with a grim recent record (8,9,0,0,0,0) and no wins from 15 runs on good or similar — Jamie Spencer can find gaps but this horse has shown very little lately and is hard to trust at any price.|

races.paceDynamic: Two Tribes is the confirmed front-runner here and, with Oisin Murphy in the saddle, will stride on from the gates to set a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 7f Newmarket straight — he is unlikely to be seriously pressured early given his natural lead. Royal Zabeel and Elarak are the most likely horses to press him prominently from the outset, with Great Acclaim and Colombier tracking closely behind, meaning the race will have a genuine early tempo without being truly scorching. The field carries a significant glut of prominent-running types — Back In Black, Christian David, and Physique are all natural front-rank horses who cannot all get their preferred position and will be forced wider or deeper than ideal, which dilutes their individual impact. With a single unhurried front-runner setting a fair but not punishing pace on good-to-firm ground at Newmarket, this race shape most favours horses who can travel prominently in the first two or three behind the leader and quicken efficiently in the final two furlongs — mid-to-high cruising speed with a sharp finish will be rewarded over pure late-closing ability.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Clean Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Two Tribes dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and the pace remains honest without acceleration until the Dip.
scenarios.body: Two Tribes bowls along in front, the field strings out at a fair tempo, and horses tracking within two lengths of the lead into the final furlong hold the decisive positional advantage; the Newmarket straight rewards those who hit the rising ground with momentum already built.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Two Tribes rolls along well within himself and the fractions are genuinely slow, compressing the field and producing a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: With the gallop too easy, the race turns into a stamina-irrelevant dash from the two-furlong pole, favouring horses with sharp acceleration and high Racing Post Ratings already in touch; prominent types who managed to hold a forward position despite the crowded nature of the field benefit most.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Two Tribes sets a brisk-enough tempo that the lead group ties up inside the final furlong, opening a late surge lane.
scenarios.body: A genuinely run race would see True hold-up horses arrive late with momentum, but this scenario is tempered by the fact that several apparent closers in this field are redistributed prominent types not ideally placed to deliver a sustained late run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Traps Favourites
scenarios.trigger: If prominent types are crowded out early and the race shape is chaotic, with no clean run for fancied horses.
scenarios.body: Redistribution of multiple prominent runners creates scrimmaging off the gate, blocking some fancied runners and gifting the race to a horse who finds a clean passage from an unfashionable position; this is the least likely outcome given the clear front-runner.

watchPoints.text: Two Tribes (Murphy) controls the pace entirely — if he quickens the tempo at the 3f pole rather than the 2f pole, horses tracking him like Elarak and Royal Zabeel gain a decisive break on the closers and the race is likely over early.

The prominent-runner squeeze — Back In Black, Christian David, and Physique all want to race forward but cannot all do so; watch the first furlong for crowding and potential interference that could compromise multiple fancied runners simultaneously.

Royal Zabeel carries the joint-top weight (143lbs) with only a 5lb claimer aboard — if Whiteley struggles to control the horse's position or conserve energy early, the top weight could blunt what is otherwise strong course-and-distance form.

Aalto (Buick) ran second over this exact trip on good going last time — if Buick gets an unimpeded passage on the stands rail in the final two furlongs, the hold-up profile and in-form jockey combination makes him a credible late threat regardless of the mapped position.

Dark Tornado's solitary win in 13 runs on good ground came over 7f at Newmarket — the combination of in-form trainer (4/5 in 14 days), course-specific form, and genuine hold-up style means he is the most credible beneficiary if the pace is strong enough to create a closing opportunity.

races.name: Boodles Superlative Stakes (Group 2)

runners_data.name: Al Hudaiba
runners_data.note: Won twice from three starts including a seven-furlong maiden at Newmarket in Good ground, giving her excellent course-and-distance form for Buick and Appleby; she is a natural front-runner and prominent racer by style, but this crowded pace scenario may push her wider in the pack than she'd prefer, tempering confidence slightly.

runners_data.name: Green Sovereign
runners_data.note: Shaped well when winning over six furlongs on Soft ground but showed less in two subsequent outings, and the step up to seven furlongs on faster going is a question mark; naturally a prominent runner, the congestion ahead means Marquand may find himself forced to settle in unfamiliar mid-division, which is against the grain of how this horse has run.

runners_data.name: Notable Dream
runners_data.note: Two runs, a third and a winner over Good ground including a Newmarket seven-furlong success, suggests the horse is already comfortable at course and distance; a prominent runner by nature, the packed pace positions mean Ghiani is likely to be racing at least partially off the pace, though the horse's Newmarket win does give some confidence this trip on this track suits.

runners_data.name: Pikachu
runners_data.note: Johnston-trained two-year-old with consecutive runs at seven furlongs at Newmarket, finishing second in the most recent outing in identical conditions — that consistent course form is a real asset; Scott can track the pace naturally from a comfortable position as one of the few horses not displaced by the redistribution.

runners_data.name: Silver Dominion
runners_data.note: One run, one win over six furlongs on Soft ground for Murphy and Cole; the sole confirmed pace-setter here, meaning Murphy will have full control of the tempo from the front, but stepping up from six to seven furlongs on faster ground having run only once is an obvious query against the class of this field.

runners_data.name: Abraham Lincoln
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore and Aidan O'Brien's sole representative, a course winner over six furlongs on Good ground at Royal Ascot — exactly the profile that Ballydoyle target Group races with; stepping up to seven furlongs is the key question but the trainer-jockey combination rarely runs blind in races of this nature, and Moore can slot him into his natural prominent position without effort.

runners_data.name: Alfred Wallace
runners_data.note: Won over seven furlongs on Good ground but has also finished fifth and twentieth in his other outings, making form hard to pin down; a naturally prominent runner by inclination, the numbers ahead of him in that position mean Loughnane is very likely to be racing out of role in mid-division, a position this horse has not demonstrated comfort in.

races.paceDynamic: Silver Dominion is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Oisin Murphy can control tempo from the front without ever being pressed — expect a true but manageable gallop on this Good to Firm Newmarket seven furlongs. Abraham Lincoln and Pikachu are the highest-rated horses and both sit naturally in a prominent position just behind the leader, meaning the pace picture directly ahead of them is uncrowded and exploitable. This field is overloaded with prominent-type runners: Notable Dream, Green Sovereign, Alfred Wallace, and Al Hudaiba are all natural front-runners or prominent racers who cannot all occupy that space, and several will be shuffled back into unfamiliar midfield slots — with Green Sovereign, Notable Dream, and Alfred Wallace most likely to cede ground and race out of role, while Al Hudaiba has enough tactical speed to potentially recover a forward position. The race shape strongly favours horses racing in their natural prominent or just-off-the-pace position — Abraham Lincoln and Pikachu are the principal beneficiaries, tracking a sustainable pace set by Silver Dominion and able to quicken at exactly the right moment.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Silver Dominion sets a fair, uncontested pace and the race is decided by horses who track him in their natural position.
scenarios.body: Silver Dominion dictates from the front without ever being seriously challenged, setting up a test of quality over raw stamina, and the prominent horses tracking him — Abraham Lincoln and Pikachu — arrive upsides with two furlongs to run in prime position to pounce. This shape rewards horses racing within themselves throughout, able to deploy a sharp finishing kick rather than grind, and both top-rated horses are ideally placed to do so.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Silver Dominion is allowed a soft lead at a pace slow enough that the prominent pack are caught flat-footed in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Murphy is never seriously threatened and the gallop is modest enough that Silver Dominion's lead turns into an unassailable advantage at the two-furlong pole, leaving the chasers with too much ground to make up in a race that failed to truly test them early. A one-run winner stepping up from a six-furlong maiden is the type to benefit from an uncontested lead on fast ground, and Silver Dominion fits that profile exactly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed prominent types crowd forward early and cause a frantic early pace before weakening, allowing a horse ridden more conservatively to finish fastest.
scenarios.body: If the early positioning battle between the many prominent-natured types causes a sharper-than-expected tempo, the field may come back to any horse ridden with restraint in the opening stages, opening a late run. Notable Dream, who won over seven furlongs at Newmarket and is racing in a natural step-up in class, is the most plausible beneficiary of an honest gallop from this pack.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Wide-Open Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Silver Dominion is outpaced early and the prominent group collectively fail to produce a clear pace shape, turning the race into a messy contest.
scenarios.body: Without a settled pace, the race becomes a sprint-like test of raw speed over the final two furlongs rather than a tactical seven-furlong contest, and any horse with a sharp finishing acceleration benefits regardless of position. Pikachu, placed twice over seven furlongs at Newmarket in similar conditions, carries sufficient class to handle the unpredictable pace scenario.

watchPoints.text: Abraham Lincoln is partnered by Ryan Moore for O'Brien and won on Good ground over six furlongs — watch whether Moore can immediately slot him into a prime tracking position behind Silver Dominion, because if he achieves that, he is perfectly placed to dominate Scenario A.

Silver Dominion has run only once, over six furlongs on Soft ground — watch the opening quarter mile closely to see whether he can maintain a genuine lead without burning out early on faster going over a longer trip, as his ability to last home is unproven.

Green Sovereign, Notable Dream, and Alfred Wallace are all natural prominent runners who cannot realistically hold that position — watch the early stages for signs of bunching or friction among this group as they jostle for space they may not all secure.

Notable Dream is 54 days between runs, the longest absence in this field — watch for any signs of freshness or greenness in the early strides, as a horse that has been off the track for nearly two months can sometimes over-race or under-race in a competitive Group 2 environment.

Pikachu is one of the very few runners whose natural prominent style is not displaced by the redistribution — watch whether Rowan Scott instinctively uses that positional advantage early, as holding the right spot without burning energy is a genuine tactical edge in this field shape.

races.name: Al Basti Equiworld, Dubai July Cup Stakes (Group 1)

runners_data.name: Almeraq
runners_data.note: Hugely consistent in-form four-year-old for Haggas and Marquand, winning four of his last seven including twice over this course and distance on Good ground; races prominently which is his natural position and the race shape suits him perfectly with Satono Reve likely to control the gallop just ahead.

runners_data.name: Big Mojo
runners_data.note: Buick takes the ride on this Appleby-trained four-year-old who has shown his best form at 6f on Good ground, but his recent record includes several disappointing efforts and he is a natural front-runner who will struggle to find his rhythm pushed further back in what is a pace-heavy prominent group.

runners_data.name: Comanche Brave
runners_data.note: O'Brien-trained four-year-old with Billy Loughnane, has won over this trip and goes well on Good ground, but the field's surplus of prominent-racers means he is unlikely to travel in his preferred position close to the pace, and his form this season has been patchy rather than progressive.

runners_data.name: Double Rush
runners_data.note: A hat-trick scorer this season for Balding and Murphy at 6f on Good ground, genuinely progressive form-wise, but his natural prominent style has pushed him to the rear on the pace map — he will need to find more room than ideal and connections must hope the pace is strong enough to bring him back into the race.

runners_data.name: Prince Of India
runners_data.note: Marco Botti's four-year-old has placed twice over 6f on Good ground but is rated 17lb below the top weight and has been out 49 days; a true prominent racer who will find himself shuffled back in a field that has too many horses wanting the same position, making his task considerably harder.

runners_data.name: Quinault
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams' six-year-old is the one genuine hold-up horse in the field, wears headgear, and has been off 59 days; his last win came over 6f on Good ground but he has been out of the frame in his most recent run and needs a truly strong pace scenario to make his challenge from off the pace.

runners_data.name: Satono Reve
runners_data.note: The key pace influence — Japan's Lemaire-ridden seven-year-old is the only confirmed front-runner, goes perfectly on Good to Firm having recorded 13 of his last 13 runs on similar going, and two consecutive second-place finishes suggest he is close to peak; his ability to dictate without being pressed makes him central to every likely race shape.

runners_data.name: Coppull
runners_data.note: Clive Cox's progressive three-year-old has won twice over 6f on Good ground and carries the three-year-old weight allowance; racing for Cox who has three winners from 21 runners over the 14-day period, but the horse's natural inclination to race prominently means he will face a difficult task finding clear air in a field crowded with similar tactical types.

runners_data.name: Division
runners_data.note: Haggas's three-year-old with James Doyle, whose best form includes a win and two thirds over 6f on Good ground; carries the three-year-old allowance but OR of 113 makes him competitive, though like several others he is a genuine prominent type who will be forced further back than ideal by the race's pace structure.

runners_data.name: Mission Central
runners_data.note: A P O'Brien's unbeaten-in-2025 three-year-old ridden by Ryan Moore, four wins from five runs on Good ground including a 6f victory, and the step up from 5f winners is untested in Group 1 company — however, the trainer's 14-day strike rate and Moore's tactical intelligence give him every chance of finding the ideal prominent berth just behind Satono Reve.

runners_data.name: Venetian Sun
runners_data.note: K R Burke's three-year-old with Clifford Lee, has won twice over 6f on Good ground recently and is on a strong upward curve with form figures of 13-011; the weight allowance for a three-year-old in a flat sprint on fast ground is a genuine asset and his prominent racing style means he should travel close enough to challenge in the final furlong.

races.paceDynamic: Satono Reve is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner Group 1 field and is likely to stride into a clear lead from the gates, setting a genuine but controlled gallop on Good to Firm ground over the Newmarket straight six. With no other horse naturally wired to press him hard from the front, he has every chance to dictate a honest but not suicidal tempo, which on fast ground over six furlongs at Newmarket typically sets up a race that rewards horses travelling smoothly in the first half and quickening off the pace rather than those grinding from deep. The field is loaded with prominent-racing types — Big Mojo, Comanche Brave, Division, Coppull, and Prince Of India are all genuine prominent horses who cannot all secure that position, and the scramble to settle into the slipstream behind Satono Reve will compress the early shape and likely crowd the three-furlong marker. This race shape — a lone leader, honest pace, fast ground — most favours horses who can sit two to four lengths off the leader travelling well and produce a clean, decisive burst in the final two furlongs; prominent-to-midfield horses with a high cruising speed and a sharp finishing kick hold the structural advantage here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Satono Reve Dictates, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Satono Reve leads uncontested and the prominent horses directly behind settle and quicken cleanly in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Satono Reve controls the race from the front on a true pace, and the horses who slot in just behind him — Almeraq, Mission Central, Venetian Sun — are ideally placed to strike as the field fans wide entering the final furlong on fast ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outlasts Field
scenarios.trigger: If Satono Reve's pace is conservative enough that no horse behind him builds sufficient momentum to reel him in.
scenarios.body: With little early pressure, Satono Reve dictates an uncontested rhythm and proves impossible to catch as rivals fail to quicken past him on Good to Firm ground; his strong recent form with two consecutive placed efforts and a win makes this entirely plausible.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Late Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the scramble for prominent positions burns out several of the prominent types and the pace proves too strong in the middle, creating a late opening.
scenarios.body: Quinault, racing from off the pace as a genuine hold-up horse, would be the primary beneficiary of a race that blows up in front, while Double Rush — though redistributed back — could also pick up late ground; this scenario is discounted because there are no true deep closers in this field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Competitive Bunched Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong, all prominent types are compressed together, and the finish is a mass sprint.
scenarios.body: Multiple horses hit the line together in a blanket finish with the winner decided by a bob of the head; fresher, lightly-weighted three-year-olds like Mission Central and Venetian Sun, carrying 6lb less, may gain a marginal edge in this scenario.

watchPoints.text: Satono Reve's lead: if Lemaire dictates a truly uncontested and comfortable tempo through the first three furlongs, the advantage this gives him in a strong-pace race on fast ground cannot be understated — watch the early splits as the key indicator of whether he is winnable or catchable.

Prominent traffic: Big Mojo, Comanche Brave, Coppull, Division and Prince Of India all want to race close to the pace — watch for significant crowding and bumping in the early furlongs as these horses contest the same stretch of ground behind Satono Reve.

Mission Central's trip: Ryan Moore's mount is unbeaten in 2025 but has won no further than 5f before today's step to 6f — watch for any sign of him flattening out in the final furlong if the pace proves sharper than his stamina can handle at Group 1 level.

Double Rush's draw and position: Balding's hat-trick scorer is a genuine prominent type placed reluctantly at the rear of the pace map — watch where Murphy positions him in the early stages; if he can sneak into a midfield berth on the inside, his chance improves materially over the mapped scenario.

Good to Firm caveat: the going report consistently shows Good to Firm for the 4:35 race despite the race card listing Good — confirm the actual underfoot conditions pre-race as Satono Reve has all 13 recent runs on similar ground while some rivals have question marks on faster surfaces.

races.name: Debenhams Handicap

runners_data.name: Sword
runners_data.note: Consistent at this trip on Good ground (2nd 7f Good recently) but a natural front-runner who will be pushed off his favoured position by the volume of pace in this field — Marco Ghiani must manage a compromised role, which dims his prospects in this particular shape.

runners_data.name: Nikovo
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old veteran whose four-timer for Herrington over 14 days shows freshness, but his Good-ground 7f record is modest (0W0P in similar conditions) and being shuffled into a midfield role strips away the tactical edge he relies upon.

runners_data.name: Leadman
runners_data.note: Excellent course form at 7f on Good (1st and 2nd here in recent starts) makes him the most course-savvy of the reshuffled prominent group; Jamie Spencer's tactical intelligence is a genuine asset if a gap materialises, though he must overcome the squeeze for early position.

runners_data.name: Righthere Rightnow
runners_data.note: Saffie Osborne takes a genuine hold-up type with a solid pattern of placed efforts at 6f on Good, stepping to 7f here — the extra furlong is a slight question mark, but a truly run race would suit this horse's ability to close off a strong pace.

runners_data.name: Harlequin Angel
runners_data.note: Jane Chapple-Hyam's three-year-old has won twice on Good at 7f and finished third on debut over 6f in similar company — Alexandra Egan claims 7lb, the form line reads 310-10 suggesting alternating runs, and this horse holds a natural prominent style that fits this race shape snugly.

runners_data.name: Rogue Messiah
runners_data.note: Won a 6f Goodwood handicap last time and placed twice on similar ground at Sandown, so the step to 7f at Newmarket is the key question; Daniel Muscutt takes the ride for a trainer in solid recent form (9/55 over 14 days), and a prominent run from a clean draw would suit.

runners_data.name: Secret History
runners_data.note: William Buick partners a horse with a strong recent form line (wins at 6f and 7f), but Ed Walker's filly is a natural prominent type shunted to the rear by field congestion — Buick will have to manufacture a run from further back than ideal, and this positional compromise is a genuine risk against a controlled pace.

runners_data.name: Glen Nevis
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old (just three career starts) with a consistent placed record on Good ground at 7-8f for Charlie Johnston; unknown style mapped as uncertain, Rowan Scott must find a rhythm quickly, and inexperience in a busy field is the primary concern.

runners_data.name: Crimson Spirit
runners_data.note: The race's structural fulcrum — sole confirmed front-runner on good 7f form at Newmarket (12 career runs on similar ground, 4 wins), carrying top weight of 142lbs for Kubler who is quiet over 14 days; the uncontested lead is the asset, but the high weight and a trainer out of current form are the offsets.

runners_data.name: Exposure
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore on a Gosden four-year-old who won on Soft/Heavy ground and is yet to prove himself on Good to Firm — the going is listed as Good to Firm for this race and his sim-going record reads 0W0P in comparable conditions, which is a legitimate flag despite the formidable rider-trainer combination.

runners_data.name: Pinatubo's Legacy
runners_data.note: Returning from a 175-day absence with only three career starts, won last time on Standard at 7f and is a natural prominent type; Tom Marquand takes the ride for a small yard (1/2 over 14 days) and the significant layoff in a competitive handicap makes this a speculative profile until much more is known.

races.paceDynamic: Crimson Spirit is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to push them off the front, Billy Loughnane can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over this Good to Firm Newmarket 7f. The field is loaded with natural prominent types — Sword, Nikovo, Leadman, Pinatubo's Legacy, Harlequin Angel, Rogue Messiah, and Exposure are all drawn from the same pace well, meaning several will be forced to sit closer to midfield than they would naturally prefer, compressing the pack behind Crimson Spirit rather than forming a genuine pace battle. Secret History is mapped to the rear despite being a prominent type, simply because the field has no room for her at the head of affairs, so William Buick will likely have to manufacture a run from further back than ideal. With a single honest gallop set by Crimson Spirit and a congested mid-pack unable to apply real pressure, this race shape heavily favours horses that can travel prominently in a box seat just off the leader and produce a decisive move entering the final two furlongs — true prominent racers who get a clean position and jockeys disciplined enough not to be squeezed out will hold the structural edge over closers who are not genuinely hold-up types by nature.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Crimson Spirit Dictates Clean
scenarios.trigger: If Crimson Spirit leads uncontested, controls the tempo, and the prominent pack behind fails to apply meaningful pressure.
scenarios.body: Loughnane slots into a rhythm on Good to Firm ground that suits this horse's 7f Newmarket record, and with the field bunching in his wake, the leader is never seriously threatened until the final furlong where a kick from the front could prove decisive. Horses who manage to track in the slipstream just off the pace — particularly those with a genuine prominent style — are best placed to pounce, but the front-runner's uncontested lead gives a material structural advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Box-Seat Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Crimson Spirit sets a fair pace but a prominent tracker travelling strongly in second or third delivers a decisive challenge in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: The compressed prominent pack means the best-positioned tracker — one who secures a clear run and travels well — can time a challenge to arrive at the death with more in reserve than a front-runner who has done all the donkey work. Harlequin Angel or Rogue Messiah, both genuine prominent types with recent winning form at this trip, are the profiles most likely to execute this move on Good to Firm ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Causes Carnage Mid-Race
scenarios.trigger: If the over-abundance of prominent types jostles for position early, inadvertently pushing the pace beyond sustainable and opening the race up for a finisher.
scenarios.body: Several natural front-runners forced into unnatural positions could create friction and a faster-than-expected tempo, flattening the leader and leaving a gap for any horse with a genuine late gear. However, Secret History is not a true hold-up type despite being mapped to the rear, so genuine closers are thin on the ground and this scenario's beneficiaries are limited in number.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Lone Front-Runner Swamped Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely too slow and a wall of prominent horses launches simultaneously inside the final furlong to overhaul Crimson Spirit.
scenarios.body: A truly crawling tempo would bring the whole field into play at once, creating a blanket finish in which the highest-rated or freshest horse could nail the post. This scenario is unlikely given Good to Firm ground encourages honest galloping fractions, but Exposure under Ryan Moore or Pinatubo's Legacy on a significant absence could exploit it if conditions conspire.

watchPoints.text: Harlequin Angel — if Alexandra Egan secures a box-seat position just off Crimson Spirit in the first two furlongs, this horse's two wins on identical Good 7f conditions make her the most dangerous individual in the race to the front-runner.

Pinatubo's Legacy — 175 days off the track is a significant welfare flag; watch for any market support or absence of it at the off, as Tom Marquand being booked for a yard with a 1/2 strike rate suggests connections may know more than the form book reveals.

Exposure — Ryan Moore's presence demands respect but the horse's Going record on Good to Firm is 0W0P across four similar-condition starts; if the ground is riding quicker than the official Good rating, monitor whether Moore rides with confidence or conserves energy.

Leadman — Jamie Spencer is adept at finding positions in crowded prominent fields and Leadman's course-and-distance record (two wins at Newmarket 7f Good) is the strongest in the field among the reshuffled prominent group; watch for Spencer to begin manoeuvring for rail position before the stalls open.

Crimson Spirit — if this horse dwells in the stalls or is slow away, the entire race shape collapses; any hesitation at the break means two or three natural front-runners immediately take over and a very different, faster-paced race develops that would dramatically change the scenario probabilities.

races.name: HKJC World Pool Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Melek Alreeh
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with solid recent form (won 162 days ago, placed twice in similar going at Sandown), David Simcock's patient handler of a horse that clearly needs a true pace over 12f+; the step up to 1m4f is the key asset here and good-to-firm suits, though the 162-day absence from the track is worth monitoring for sharpness.

runners_data.name: Wonder
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with a clear lead role tonight, but the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) signals it rarely wins from this position; James Fanshawe's five-year-old has placed consistently at 12f on Soft-to-Standard going but good-to-firm is a slight unknown (only 1 from 15 in similar going), and D'Arcy's 7lb claim is a useful weight offset.

runners_data.name: First Officer
runners_data.note: Jane Chapple-Hyam's veteran has genuine prominent inclinations, but with Cape Fear and Wonder already ahead of it in the queue, it is likely to race further back than it naturally wants; the 1 win from 15 on similar going suggests it can handle the surface, and Moldoveanu's claim (7lb) keeps the weight manageable, but racing against type undermines its chance.

runners_data.name: Bintabuha
runners_data.note: Harry Charlton's four-year-old is a true hold-up type nudged into a midfield position on the map, and its recent form at 10f on good ground (back-to-back fifth placings) raises questions about whether 1m4f truly suits; Tom Marquand's horsemanship is an asset, but the combination of an unfamiliar trip and a style mismatch warrants caution — the 1W3P record in similar going provides modest encouragement.

runners_data.name: Cape Fear
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's three-year-old has an excellent record in similar conditions (6/6 sim-going, 1W5P) and arrives on a tight 23-day turnaround in good form; Oisin Murphy will likely sit prominently behind Wonder, which is a natural and comfortable position for this horse, and the class edge of a younger stayer tackling older rivals for the first time is the key unknown.

runners_data.name: Parisian Scholar
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's three-year-old arrives fresh (10 days), in cracking recent form (won 12f/Good last time), and runs for a trainer in flying shape (9/78 over 14 days); Rowan Scott is a capable claimer and the hold-up profile suits a race likely to be set up by Wonder — the inconsistent broader form string (including an 11th) is the only brake on enthusiasm.

races.paceDynamic: Wonder is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with only six runners over 1m4f at Newmarket on good-to-firm ground, Arron D'Arcy (7) should be able to dictate an honest but controlled gallop that never becomes truly searching. Cape Fear and First Officer are also prominent-minded, meaning the early order will be competitive enough to establish a genuine tempo, but Wonder is unlikely to be harassed into something unsustainably fast. This field holds more prominent types than can all occupy the rail in a small field — First Officer and Bintabuha, both redistributed on the pace map, are unlikely to secure their natural positions and will compromise their chances by racing against type. The sustainable, metronomic gallop set by Wonder on fast ground over this stamina trip strongly favours hold-up horses with a genuine staying kick — Melek Alreeh and Parisian Scholar are best placed to exploit a well-run but unfrenetic pace that sets up a decisive late surge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Wonder Controls, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Wonder dictates a fair but uncontested gallop and the race is run at a true staying tempo without any serious early pressure.
scenarios.body: Wonder sets fractions that suit stayers, allowing Melek Alreeh and Parisian Scholar to glide through from the rear in the final two furlongs; good-to-firm ground rewards those with a clean finishing stride rather than those who have already spent energy fighting for position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Cape Fear Stalks And Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Cape Fear tracks Wonder closely throughout, saving ground from second or third, and kicks decisively off the home turn.
scenarios.body: Cape Fear's consistent form at 10-12f on good ground (6/6 in similar going) and young legs as a three-year-old give it a tactical edge when racing prominently in a small field; Oisin Murphy's positioning will be crucial in a race this size.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Rear Runners Swamp
scenarios.trigger: If Wonder's gallop is so uncontested that the pace becomes falsely slow and those in front wind it up late, causing a sprint finish that negates the hold-up runners.
scenarios.body: A falsely-run affair over 1m4f on fast ground compresses the finish and benefits those nearest the pace who can quicken sharply; Wonder and Cape Fear are best-placed to capitalise if the race turns into a short-home test.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos, Prominent Battle
scenarios.trigger: If First Officer pushes forward against type and sets up a contested pace with Wonder, injecting more early pressure than expected.
scenarios.body: A genuinely strong gallop could see the field string out earlier than anticipated, and any hold-up horse that travels sweetly could mop up a tiring front rank; however, First Officer and Bintabuha racing against their natural styles reduces this scenario's reliability.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Cape Fear, ridden by Oisin Murphy, can slot into second behind Wonder immediately — if Murphy secures the prime stalking position, Cape Fear becomes the most dangerous horse in the race given its 6/6 record on similar ground.

Monitor Wonder's early fractions via Arron D'Arcy (7): if the pace is conspicuously slow through the first half-mile in a field of only six, the race could turn into a sprint home that negates Melek Alreeh and Parisian Scholar entirely.

First Officer is likely to be shuffled wider and further back than ideal if Cape Fear and Wonder fill the prominent berths — Moldoveanu (7) will need to manage this carefully or the horse burns energy fighting for position against its instincts.

Parisian Scholar ran only 10 days ago; watch in the paddock for any signs of fatigue or sweat — Johnston and Scott clearly intend to ride the horse fresh off a recent win, but back-to-back quick returns can show in the ring on fast ground.

Bintabuha has not raced beyond 12f in its last five starts; watch the sectionals in the final quarter-mile to see if the extra distance tests its stamina, as any late wobble would confirm the trip concern flagged by its recent form profile.
